articles.title: Liquid Glass in the Browser: Refraction with CSS and SVG
articles.description: A superb, solid exploration of how to approach recreating Apple’s Liquid Glass effect on the web using CSS, SVG displacement maps, and physics-based refraction calculations. Good, informative visuals here and a playground to see things in action. Demos are Chrome-only right now.
articles.author: Chris Feijoo

articles.title: 🎨 Color Shifting in CSS
articles.description: Changing the shape or position of something is a common focus in Web animations, but what about smooth and attractive color shifting too? Josh shares what he knows about it, some color space quirks, and how to keep things quick using CSS filters.
articles.author: Josh W. Comeau

articles.title: Make Your Proposals for Interop 2026
articles.description: The feature submission form for Interop 2026 proposals is now open until later this month. Here Rachel outlines what makes a good submission for the future, and shares a quick update on 2025 progress. Jen Simmons of the WebKit team has also shared some notes on the process.
articles.author: Rachel Andrew

articles.title: What You Need to Know About CSS Color Interpolation
articles.description: Color interpolation is, in essence determining the colors between two color points, and here Sunkanmi shares how we can use this with various CSS properties and functions, be that via gradients, transitions, or direct mixing.
articles.author: Sunkanmi Fafowora

articles.title: Low and Mid-Tier Mobile for the Real World
articles.description: What devices would constitute as a real-life low or mid-tier mobile in 2025? How would such devices map to a Chrome DevTools presets? Considering that not everyone is using the very latest and greatest iPhone, Harry investigates.
articles.author: Harry Roberts

articles.title: The Fundamentals of CSS Alignment
articles.description: An exploration of the logic behind all alignment properties (not just entering!) and how they work in each layout.
articles.author: Temani Afif

articles.title: “Your” vs “My” in User Interfaces
articles.description: When labelling items in your UI which should you use (My Account, Your Orders, etc), and do you even need them at all?
articles.author: Adam Silver

articles.title: How AI Is Changing Search Behaviors
articles.description: Generative AI isn’t replacing search, but it is reshaping it, becoming a growing part of how people now look for information.
articles.author: Moran, Rosala, Brown (NNg)

articles.title: Why You Should Test Your Page Without JavaScript
articles.description: Highlights the reasons why JS can fail, what progressive enhancements we can put in place, and what scenarios are possible outliers.
articles.author: Ilknur Eren

articles.title: Pokémon Cards CSS Holographic Effect
articles.description: Yep, I still collect Pokémon cards, so this is like shiny catnip to me. A bunch of demos using advanced CSS to create rather accurate, realistic-looking effects. There’s 3D transforms, CSS gradients, blend modes and more. Cool!
articles.author: Simon Goellner

articles.title: Announcing Reciprocate, A Sweet Solution for Making Your HTML Web Components Reactive
articles.description: A helper utility for adding signal-based reactivity and attribute/property reflection to any vanilla custom element class. There’s a demo here, and the repo is here.
articles.author: Jared White

articles.title: Peaks.js 4.0: UI Component for Interacting with Audio Waveforms
articles.description: A project originally spawned from the BBC’s R&D department, Peaks renders audio waveforms to a canvas element and allows scrolling, zooming, and the sort of things you might otherwise see in an audio editor. LGPL licensed.
articles.author: Chris Needham et al.

articles.title: Splide: Lightweight and Accessible Slider/Carousel
articles.description: It’s nice to see a clean, modern spin on the often maligned UI element. The homepage is packed with demos too. No dependencies, written in TypeScript, and boasts a clean report from Lighthouse. GitHub repo.
articles.author: Naotoshi Fujita

articles.title: mdream: Convert Any Site to Clean Markdown & llms.txt
articles.description: Ostensibly for boosting a site’s AI discoverability, among other things.
articles.author: Harlan Wilton

articles.title: Cosmic UI: A Curated Set of Futuristic UI Components
articles.description: Sci-gi fans will love this one. The customizable framework-agnostic components use SVG for some of the unique shapes and the functionality is powered by the Zag library. Repo here.
articles.author: muhammad rizki
